source.topic: Mike Tyson's boxing life: discipline, championship, adversity, and reinvention
source.source_text: Factual notes for a documentary about Mike Tyson. He was born in Brooklyn, New York, in 1966. As a teenager, a counselor and former boxer introduced him to trainer Cus D’Amato, who became Tyson’s coach and legal guardian. Tyson won Junior Olympic gold medals in 1981 and 1982, made his professional debut in 1985, and won his first nineteen professional bouts by knockout. D’Amato died in 1985 before Tyson won a world heavyweight title. In 1986 Tyson won the WBC heavyweight title at age twenty, becoming the youngest heavyweight champion in boxing history. He won additional heavyweight titles and unified three major titles in 1987. His first professional defeat came in 1990. In 1992 he was convicted of rape in Indiana and received a prison sentence; he was released on parole in 1995. He returned to boxing, regained heavyweight titles in 1996, and lost one later that year. In a 1997 rematch he was disqualified after biting his opponent’s ears; the Nevada commission revoked his boxing license and later restored it. In 2002 a heavyweight opponent knocked him out. At the end of 2005 his reported record was 50 wins, 6 losses, 2 no contests, and 44 knockouts. Muhammad Ali, Sugar Ray Robinson, and Joe Frazier are major historical figures in boxing and may appear only as contextual reference points, not as people Tyson fought or trained with. Distinguish athletic achievement from personal harm and legal accountability. Do not invent direct quotations or claim that sporting results define a whole life.
